<result>I found fewer path fields than the request expected. There is no form input for a clone destination, a Dockerfile path, an SSH key path, a scan target or a template destination. The forge clone code in `internal/ui/forge/explorer/clone_list.go` has no destination field. Template scans write to a fixed folder (`internal/template/materialize.go:15`). The SSH key is only mentioned in help text (`internal/ui/setup/fields.go:123`). Scan targets come from rows the user selects, not from typing.

## A. Path fields that do exist

### A1. Configuration view (`:cfg`)
One shared `textinput.Model` serves every text field in this view. It is not one input per field and not a `WrappedInput`.

- **Input:** declared at `internal/ui/configuration/model.go:57`, created at `model.go:130` (`CharLimit = 512`).
- **Binding:** `bindInput()` at `internal/ui/configuration/update.go:399` loads the focused field's value into the input with `SetValue(f.Value(cfg))`, `CursorEnd` and `Focus`. `resizeInput()` sets the width from the column width.
- **Field model:** a `field` struct with a `fieldKind` enum at `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:17-39` (`kindText`, `kindInteger`, `kindToggle`, `kindCycle`, `kindStatic`, `kindSecret`). The `text()` and `validated()` constructors are at `fields.go:123` and `:127`, and `field.validate func(string) error` is at `:97`.
- **Focus:** `Model.activeTab` and `focusedField int` index into `sections[activeTab].Fields`.
- **Keys:** `handleKey` at `update.go:64`. Tab switches tabs, up/down move between fields (`moveField` at `:118`), left/right cycle values. Changes are written when the field loses focus, via `commitFocused` (around `update.go:209`) and then `field.Apply` at `fields.go:256`.
- **Rendering:** `renderField(f field, focused bool)` at `internal/ui/configuration/view.go:299`. A focused text field shows `KeyStyle(prefix) + m.input.View()`. An unfocused one shows the raw `f.Value(cfg)` with no shortening.

| Field | Location | Validation | `~` expansion |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Workspaces dir" (`App.WorkspacesDir`) | `fields.go:310` | `Apply` only trims spaces; no `validate` function | Not in the form. Expanded when the config loads (`config.go:819`). The dashboard and workspaces views also expand it themselves (see B) |
| "Config file" (static, read-only) | `fields.go:315` | n/a | Absolute path from `config.GetContextPath` |
| "Log file" (`App.LogFile`) | `fields.go:316` | trim only | Only when the config loads (`config.go:818`) |
| "IDE command" / "Terminal command" | `fields.go:324,326` | trim only | none (these are commands, but may contain paths) |
| Per-tool "Binary" (`scan.Tools[id].Binary`) | `internal/ui/configuration/scan_fields.go:243` | trim only | Only when the config loads (`config.go:824`) |
| Per-tool "Config" (rules file; only if `tool.HasConfig`) | `scan_fields.go:249`, hint "Path to a rules file, made absolute when saved" | trim only | Only when the config loads: `absolute(expand(...))` at `config.go:825`, with `absolute()` at `config.go:841` |

Four things to know about this view:
- `Apply` (`fields.go:256-281`) stores `strings.TrimSpace(raw)` as typed. It never expands `~`.
- `config.SaveContext` (`internal/config/config.go:853`) marshals the config as it is. So a typed `~/foo` is written to the file literally and stays literal in memory until the next load, when `ExpandPaths` (`config.go:810-827`, called at `:802`) expands it.
- After any load the in-memory values are absolute, so the form shows paths like `/home/anthoni/...`. Nothing folds them back to `~`.
- The Config field's hint says "made absolute when saved", but that actually happens at load time.

### A2. Template catalog form: the Path field
The `path` input is a `textinput.Model`. Its label changes with the source kind.

- **Declaration:** `internal/ui/templates/form.go:39` (`name, tags, url, path, ref textinput.Model`). The description field is a `sharedcomponents.WrappedInput` at `:40`.
- **Construction:** `newInput("", 300)` at `form.go:62`, helper at `:88` (width 60, `theme.StyleTextInput`).
- **Field enum:** `formField` at `form.go:18-29` (`fieldName`, `fieldDescription`, `fieldTags`, `fieldKind`, `fieldURL`, `fieldPath`, `fieldRef`, `fieldSubmit`). The focus value is an index into `fields()` (`:108`), and `fieldURL` is left out for the local kind.
- **Keys:** `Update` at `form.go:150`. Up/down move, Enter moves to the next field or submits, left/right cycle the kind, Tab does nothing, other keys go to `forward()` at `:201`.
- **Rendering:** `View()` at `:292` calls `line(field, label, value)` at `:345`. Labels come from `labels()` at `:333`: "Directory" for the local kind, "Subdirectory" for git, "Repository" for OCI.
- **Validation:** `entry()` at `form.go:221` then `Source.Validate()` at `internal/template/template.go:75`. For the local kind it only checks that the path is not empty (`:81-84`), and it rejects a leading `-` (`:95-99`).
- **`~` expansion:** none. The path goes straight to `git.ArchiveLocal(ctx, src.Path, ...)` (`internal/template/fetch.go:106`, `internal/git/archive.go:18`), which runs git with `repoPath` as its working directory. A `~/x` path would fail.

### A3. Workspaces view: new folder / rename name
This is a `textinput.Model` for a name inside the current directory, not a full path.

- **Location:** `internal/ui/workspaces/input.go:22`. `NewWorkspaceInput` is at `:29` (placeholder "directory-name", CharLimit 100, width 40). `NewRenameInput` is at `:46`.
- **Focus:** an `iota` enum at `input.go:14-18` (`focusInput`, `focusCreate`, `focusCancel`).
- **Keys:** `Update` at `:77`. Up/down move focus, Enter calls `handleEnter` at `:137`, Esc cancels.
- **Rendering:** `View` at `:163`, with the label "Name".
- **Validation:** only a non-empty trimmed value. The name is joined onto the current directory in `createWorkspace` (`internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:384-403`, `MkdirAll(filepath.Join(baseDir, name))`) and in `renameEntry` (`internal/ui/workspaces/update.go:566-567`). Nothing rejects `/` or `..`, so a nested path or an escape out of the directory is possible.
- **`~` expansion:** only for the base directory, via `getExpandedWorkspacesDir` (`update.go:433-440`).

### A4. Launch form: Volumes (host path is optional)
- **Location:** `volInput textinput.Model` at `internal/ui/oci_resources/launch_form.go:81`, placeholder "myvolume:/app/data" at `:110`.
- **Focus:** `focusedField int` with methods such as `fieldVolumes()` returning 3 (`:255`).
- **Rendering:** `internal/ui/oci_resources/launch_form_render.go:178`.
- **Handling:** split on commas at `launch_form.go:482-486` and passed through as `-v` arguments (`internal/docker/launch.go:61`).
- **Validation:** none. **`~` expansion:** none.

The Entrypoint input (`launch_form.go:79`, `:108`) holds a path inside the container and is checked against the image, not the host.

## B. Existing `~` and path-shortening helpers

**Folding `$HOME` into `~`:**
- `shortenHome(path)` at `internal/ui/security/inventory_table.go:186-199` uses `filepath.Rel` against `os.UserHomeDir()`. It returns `~` or `~/rel`, and leaves paths outside home unchanged. It is used at `:124`, `:179` and `internal/ui/security/findings.go:344`. This is the only home-to-`~` helper in the codebase, and it is private to the security package.

**Expanding `~` (all duplicated, each only handles a leading `~/`):**
- `Config.ExpandPaths` at `internal/config/config.go:810-827`, called at load time (`:802`)
- `expandHome` at `internal/ui/dashboard/model.go:547`
- `getExpandedWorkspacesDir` at `internal/ui/workspaces/update.go:433`
- `readKey` in `internal/trust/policy.go:213-218` (cosign key path, relative paths resolved against the policy directory)
- `absolute()` at `internal/config/config.go:841` (`filepath.Abs`)

**Truncation (all keep the end of the path; there is no middle truncation and no fish-style abbreviation):**
- `theme.TruncateTailWidth(s, max)` at `internal/ui/theme/text.go:46`. Its doc comment says it is meant for filesystem paths, and it prefixes `theme.Ellipsis = "..."` (`text.go:8`). The grep found no callers outside `text.go`, so it appears unused.
- `theme.TruncateWidth` at `text.go:25` keeps the start and appends `...`.
- `truncatePath(path, width)` at `internal/ui/dashboard/sections.go:1175` keeps the end with a `…` prefix and measures width in terminal cells (helper `countKept` at `:1188`). It is used for WorkspacesDir at `:108` and `:136`.
- `truncateHead` at `internal/ui/datatable/render.go:165` backs the `Column.TruncateHead` option for table cells.
- `theme.Truncate(line, width)` at `internal/ui/theme/box.go:105` is a plain ANSI-safe cut, not path-aware.

**Basename:**
- `pathBaseName` at `internal/ui/workspaces/view.go:173` (`filepath.Base`) is used for the breadcrumb tabs (`:154`, `:159`) and the header's "Directory" value (`:607-609`, which falls back to a literal `"~"` at the root).

No function in `internal/` is named `Abbrev`, `Shorten`, `TruncateMiddle` or `TruncatePath`. `shortSHA` in `internal/version/version.go:117` is unrelated.</result>

<result>I've mapped all four areas. One premise needs correcting first: the security view no longer borrows workspaces. That flow was removed (`app/app.go:610-613`, `app/command_line.go:107-110`). Today the only borrower is the forge explorer, which borrows two views: workspaces (clone destination) and templates (template choice). I didn't write a plan file; everything is below.

## 1. Router (`internal/app`)

**View interfaces.** The router checks for each of these with a type assertion. None is required at compile time.
- `HeaderView` (`app_header.go:13-18`) has four methods: `GetShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts`, `GetTitle()`, `GetIcon()` and `GetHeaderInfo(context string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo`. A view that implements only some of them matches nothing and gets an empty title (`app-shell.md:202-207`).
- `FooterView` (`app_header.go:22-25`): `GetFooterHeight() int` and `RenderFooter(width int) string`. The footer height is subtracted from the viewport in `layoutOnce` (`app.go:337-363`). `forwardToActiveView` re-runs the layout when the footer height changes (`keys.go:81-92`).
- `FormView.InEditMode()` (`app.go:35-37`): while it returns true, bare `:`, `q` and `?` go to the view instead of the router (`keys.go:109-141`, `help_overlay.go:26`). `ctrl+p` always opens command mode (`keys.go:56`). `esc` always goes to the view (`keys.go:64-72`).
- Other optional interfaces: `LeavingView.Leave()` (`app.go:51-53`), `FilterBarView.FilterBarVisible()` (`app.go:58-60`), and `FramelessView` (`app_header.go:34`, dashboard only, enforced by a test).
- `help.Provider.GetHelpContent() help.Content` (`internal/ui/help/help.go:32`), used by `maybeOpenHelp` (`help_overlay.go:30`).
- Contract test: `TestEveryViewSuppliesItsHeaderAndHelp` (`view_contract_test.go:26-55`) runs over `command.AllViewNames()`. Each view needs a `createView` case, a `HeaderView`, a non-empty title, at least one shortcut, and a `help.Provider`. `TestOnlyTheDashboardIsFrameless` (`:60`) also applies.

**`:command` to view.** Everything is in `internal/command/parser.go`:
- The `ViewType` constants are at `:12-54`.
- `viewNames` (`:85-118`) is the single map from spellings (including aliases) to views, used by both parsing and completion.
- `routerViews` (`:59`) holds views with no command name, such as `viewer`. They appear in `AllViewNames()` but not `ViewNames()`.
- `ParseCommand` is at `:149-172`.
- Tests that would catch a new view:
  - `command/doc_test.go:132 TestEveryTypeableViewIsDocumented`: the bullet list in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md:43-59` must list it.
  - `completion_test.go:38/55`.
  - The configuration view's `default_view` field offers everything in `ViewNames()` (`configuration/model.go:146`).

**Switching views.**
- `runCommand` (`command_line.go:64-100`) calls `resetSelectionModeFor(view)` (`:121-138`), then `switchView` (`:141-166`).
- `switchView` first calls `settleCurrentView` / `Leave` (`:177-189`). It builds the view lazily with `createView` (`:192-232`, one `case` per view), then returns `Init()`, a resize and `sendJobsTo`.
- The view picker (Tab in command mode) follows the same path (`:277-296`).

**Cross-view messages.**
- Messages defined in the router: `SwitchViewMsg` (`messages.go:13`). Most messages are defined in the view packages and have a `case` in `App.Update` (`app.go:390-662`).
- The "open with an argument, return with esc" pattern:
  - `uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg` goes to `handleViewerOpenRequest` (`viewer.go:17-31`). It builds the view, sets `OriginView = a.currentView` and installs it.
  - `BackToOriginMsg{Origin}` goes to `switchView(msg.Origin)` (`app.go:642-643`).
  - netdiag works the same way (`netdiag.go:16-29`, `app.go:648-652`).
- Background work is routed by view name with `routeToView` / `routeWork` (`app.go:673-681`). Any `jobs.Reporter` message needs a `case` in the router, or `TestEveryJobReporterIsRoutedToTheRegistry` fails (`reporter_routes_test.go:26`).

**The existing "pick and return" flow is `internal/app/selection.go`.**
- State: `App.selectionReturnView` and `App.selectionLent` (`app.go:102-108`).
- Request:
  1. The borrower sends a request message, e.g. `explorer.CloneSelectionRequestMsg{}` (`forge/explorer/clone.go:77`).
  2. The router runs `handleExplorerCloneRequest` (`selection.go:31-38`). It saves the return view and calls `openBrowser(ViewWorkspaces, workspaces.NewForSelection(cfg, prompt))` (`:41-46`), which puts a fresh selection-mode instance into `a.views`.
- Answer:
  1. The lent view sends `workspaces.DirectorySelectedMsg{Path}` or `SelectionCancelledMsg{}`.
  2. The router's handler (`selection.go:49-60`) calls `leaveSelectionMode()` (`:85-89`), which deletes the lent view so it is rebuilt normally later.
  3. `returnToOrigin(explorer.CloneDestinationSelectedMsg{Path})` (`:92-101`) sends the answer to the borrower's `Update`.
- Each borrow has its own request/answer/cancel message types, and the router translates them into the borrower's own message types. The templates borrow repeats the pattern (`selection.go:63-81`, `app.go:626-633`).
- Typing `:workspaces` always deletes the workspaces view first (`command_line.go:122-124`), so a view left in selection mode never shows up.
- Tests: `lifecycle_test.go:417-470` (`TestTheExplorerBorrowsWorkspacesForACloneDestination`, `TestThePickedDirectoryGoesBackToTheExplorer`).
- For a generic file picker this would mean a `NewForSelection`-style constructor with options (dirs only / files allowed), one `PathSelectedMsg` / `PickCancelledMsg` pair, and a router step that turns the answer into the requester's message.

## 2. Workspaces (`internal/ui/workspaces`)

**Model and modes.**
- Modes are defined at `model.go:18-29`: Normal, Adding, ConfirmingDelete, Renaming, Selecting, ConfirmingScanAll, FuzzyFinding.
- Navigation state (`model.go:40-55`):
  - `currentPath` is `""` at the workspaces root.
  - `listingPath` guards against stale listings.
  - `navigationStack` and `cursorStack` hold the path and cursor for each level.
  - `pendingCursor` and `pendingSelectPath` restore the cursor after a load.
- `New` is at `:165-177`. `NewForSelection(cfg, message)` (`:182-187`) sets `ModeSelecting` and the prompt.
- `Entry` (`:133-159`) mixes filesystem fields (Name, Path, ModTime, IsDir) with git fields.

**Navigation (`update.go`).**
- `→` calls `navigateIn` (`:357-377`). It refuses while `listingPath != currentPath`, pushes onto the stacks, then runs `loadEntries`.
- `←` and `esc` call `navigateUp` (`:380-404`).
- The key switch is at `:275-316`.
- `EntriesLoadedMsg` / `LoadErrorMsg` stamped with a different path are dropped (`:62-96`).
- In selection mode (`:407-430`), `enter` picks the directory being browsed, not the highlighted row. `esc` goes up one level and cancels only at the root.
- The root is `getExpandedWorkspacesDir()` (`:433-440`), which expands `~/` itself. Navigation cannot go above the workspaces root, and `jumpToPath` also bails out if the target is outside it (`:478-485`).

**Listing (`table.go:61-126`).**
- `loadEntries` is a Cmd that captures its values before running (Rule 110). It creates the root if missing, then `os.ReadDir`.
- Hidden entries are filtered with `isHidden(name, cfg.App.ShowHiddenFiles)` (`entry.go:22-24`).
- `IsDir` comes from `leadsToDir`, which follows symlinks and junctions (`entry.go:261-270`).
- Every directory is passed to `enrichEntry`, which runs git status and a recursive walk for nested repos (`entry.go:27-36`, `139-197`). That is expensive and a file browser doesn't need it.

**Create (`N`).**
- `startAdd` (`update.go:443-447`) opens `NewWorkspaceInput()` (`input.go:29-43`). `WorkspaceInput` is a package-local text input with Create/Cancel buttons and ↑↓ focus. It emits `WorkspaceInputSubmitMsg{Name}` / `WorkspaceInputCancelMsg` (`:68-74`). The same component in rename mode emits `RenameInputSubmitMsg` (`:46-61`).
- `handleInputSubmit` calls `createWorkspace` (`actions.go:384-404`), which does `MkdirAll(filepath.Join(base, name))`. The result comes back as `WorkspaceCreatedMsg` and triggers a reload (`update.go:614-620`).
- Two defects worth not copying:
  - The closure reads `m.currentPath` at run time (`actions.go:389`) instead of capturing it, which breaks Rule 110.
  - The name is only `TrimSpace`d (`input.go:140`). `a/b` or `../x` is accepted, and `MkdirAll` would create nested directories or write outside the browsed directory.
- `N` is deliberately never greyed (`availability.go:33-40`).

**Delete (`D`).**
- `startDelete` (`update.go:515-541`) checks `busy`, stores `pendingEntry` and opens `components.NewConfirmModal(title, msg)`. The title is "Delete File" or "Delete Directory".
- The modal is in `components/confirm_modal.go`:
  - It defaults to No.
  - ←/→ toggle, enter or space confirm the focused button.
  - `y/Y` and `n/N/esc` answer directly.
  - It emits `ConfirmModalYesMsg` / `ConfirmModalNoMsg`.
- `handleConfirmDelete` (`update.go:593-611`) checks `busy` again, then `jobs.Start(m.deleteRun(path), m.deleteEntry(path))`.
  - `deleteEntry` is `os.RemoveAll` (`actions.go:412-416`).
  - `deleteRun` uses `jobs.KindDelete` with owner `command.ViewWorkspaces` (`jobs.go:35-37`).
  - `EntryDeletedMsg` implements `jobs.Reporter` (`jobs.go:173-191`) and is routed at `app.go:551-554`.
  - A new view doing the same needs its own Reporter message and a router `case`.

**Rename (`M`):** `startRename` → `NewRenameInput` → `renameEntry` (`os.Rename`) → `EntryRenamedMsg` (`update.go:544-583`).

**Availability pattern (`availability.go`).**
- `actionState = shortcut.Availability` (`:22`); `available` and `unavailable(reason)` are defined at `:26-29`.
- `actionSet` (`:41-50`) and the reason constants (`:54-61`) sit beside `actions()` (`:74-148`), which works out each key's state from the selected row.
- `guard(state, act)` (`:155-160`) refuses a greyed key with `footer.Warn(reason)`.
- `GetShortcuts` greys from the same set (`view.go:567-592`). Handlers use `m.guard(a.X, ...)` (`update.go:273-306`).
- Tests are in `availability_test.go` (130 lines).

**datatable usage.**
- `datatable.New(datatable.Config[workspaceRow]{Columns, SortColumn:-1})` (`model.go:169-172`).
- Columns are in `columns.go:122-190`. The first is an untitled glyph column of width `datatable.IconColumnWidth`, with `Cell: entryIcon` and `Style: theme.IconStyle(entryIconRole)`. Then Name (`SizingContent`, has `Search`), and so on.
- `Column` fields are documented at `datatable/datatable.go:57-171`. `Sizing` is mandatory, and a test rejects a column without it.
- API calls used by the view: `SetItems` + `Remeasure` (`table.go:23-26`), `Selected()` (`:55-58`), `Resize(w, h-1)` (`:15-17`), `SetCursor`, `FilterBar()`, `InEditMode()`, and `Update(msg)` for up/down/pgup/pgdown/home/end and `/`.

**fileicon.**
- `fileicon.For(name) string` (`fileicon/fileicon.go:244-260`) checks the basename first, then the `dockerfile.` and `readme.` prefixes, then the extension, and falls back to `theme.IconFile`. It never returns empty.
- It is already its own package with no dependencies besides `theme`, so it can be reused directly.
- Workspaces wraps it in `entryIcon` / `entryIconRole` (`view.go:271-302`), which choose between repository, directory and file.

**Footer and help.**
- `GetFooterHeight` / `RenderFooter` (`view.go:98-136`) render the filter bar, then the breadcrumb tab bar (`renderTabBar` `:149-163`, `theme.RenderTabs`), then a blank line, then the info line from `components.FooterMessage`.
- Selection mode renders the tab bar plus the prompt (`:115-117`).
- Help content is at `view.go:619-697`.

**Can the listing logic be reused?** Not as it stands.
- Everything is unexported in package `workspaces`: `loadEntries`, `isHidden`, `leadsToDir`, `holdsRepo`/`isRepo`, `mayFollow`, `pathBaseName`.
- The load returns workspaces-specific messages (`EntriesLoadedMsg`, `LoadErrorMsg`), is tied to `Model.currentPath` and the workspaces root, and always runs git enrichment.
- A new view would need to either extract a small domain package (for example `internal/fsbrowse` with `List(dir, showHidden) ([]Entry, error)`, `LeadsToDir`, `IsHidden`) and have workspaces call it, or copy the code. Copying would break the "one rule for hidden entries" invariant described at `entry.go:12-21`.

# §3.95 — File browser view (`:files`) + path picker for forms

## Context

DevDesk has no general-purpose file browser. The `ws` view only browses under the
workspaces root, and it carries a lot of git logic (`enrichEntry`). Form fields that
expect a path — `:cfg` Workspaces dir / Log file / scanner Binary / scanner Config,
and `:templates` local Path — are free text only. Nothing expands `~` in the form,
nothing checks that the path exists, and an unfocused field shows the full absolute
path, which pushes the form's layout wide.

What we are building:
1. A **`:files` view** that browses the whole filesystem (starting in `$HOME`, with
   `←` going up to `/`). It can create a file or directory (`N`) and delete one
   (`D`, confirmation defaults to No).
2. The same view in **picker mode**, opened from a **`[ Browse… ]` button**
   focusable right after each path field (`↓` then `Enter`, per Rule 135).
3. A **short form of a path** for display: `$HOME` becomes `~`, then intermediate
   segments are reduced fish-style (`~/p/w/a/devdesk`). The final name is always
   kept whole, and a leading `…` is the last resort.

Decisions made with the user: Browse button (not Enter on the field), fish-style,
full filesystem scope, all five fields in this first batch.

Work in a worktree: `git worktree add -b feat/file-browser .worktrees/feat/file-browser origin/main`.

## 1. Domain: extract the listing — `internal/fsbrowse` (new)

Move out of `internal/ui/workspaces/entry.go` what is not git: `isHidden`,
`leadsToDir` (follows symlinks and junctions), `mayFollow`. Then add:

```go
type Entry struct{ Name, Path string; IsDir bool; Size int64; ModTime time.Time; Mode fs.FileMode }
func List(dir string, showHidden bool) ([]Entry, error)   // os.ReadDir + LeadsToDir, sorted dirs-first
func IsHidden(name string, show bool) bool
func LeadsToDir(path string, d fs.DirEntry) bool
func ValidName(name string) error                         // not empty, no separator, not "." / "..", no NUL
func Create(dir, name string, isDir bool) (string, error) // ValidName + O_EXCL / Mkdir (never MkdirAll)
func Remove(path string) error                            // RemoveAll, refuses "/" and $HOME
func NearestExisting(path string) string                  // start of the picker
func ExpandHome(p string) string                          // single implementation of "~/"
```

`workspaces` calls `fsbrowse.IsHidden`/`LeadsToDir`, which keeps the "one rule for
hidden entries" invariant (`entry.go:12-21`). **Optional in the same PR**: have
`createWorkspace` go through `fsbrowse.ValidName`. It fixes the `a/b` / `../x` hole
spotted in `workspaces/input.go:140`, which is a defect to record in backlog §1.1.

Tests: table-driven `ValidName`, `Create` refusing an existing entry, and `List` on
`t.TempDir()` (hidden entries, symlink to a directory, sort order).

## 2. Display: `theme.ShortPath` — `internal/ui/theme/path.go` (new)

```go
func FoldHome(path string) string               // moved from security/inventory_table.go:186 (shortenHome)
func ShortPath(path string, maxWidth int) string // FoldHome → fish left to right → leading "…" + tail
```

Algorithm: if `StringWidth(fold) <= max`, return it. Otherwise reduce each
intermediate segment to its first rune, starting from the left (a hidden segment
keeps its dot: `.devdesk` becomes `.d`), stopping as soon as the path fits. If it
still does not fit, keep the last segment and fall back to `TruncateTailWidth`.
Measurement uses `runewidth`, not `len`. Windows: separator `filepath.Separator`,
and the volume `C:` is kept.

`security` switches to `theme.FoldHome` (3 call sites). The dashboard's
`truncatePath` (`dashboard/sections.go:1175`) is left alone and noted as a later
convergence.

Table tests: fits as is, fish reduction in stages, final name too long, `~` alone,
path outside home, hidden segment, multibyte runes.

## 3. The view — `internal/ui/filebrowser` (new)

Follow the model of `ws` (`internal/ui/workspaces`) without its git logic:
- `model.go`: `Model{config, mode, currentPath, listingPath, cursorStack, table datatable.Model[fsbrowse.Entry], footer components.FooterMessage, confirm *components.ConfirmModal, form *createForm, pick *PickRequest}`.
  Modes are Normal, Creating, ConfirmingDelete and Picking. The stale-listing guard
  mirrors `ws` (`listingPath`).
- `table.go`: the `loadEntries` Cmd **captures** `dir` and `showHidden` before its
  closure (Rule 110; do not copy the `actions.go:389` defect). It emits
  `EntriesLoadedMsg{Dir, Entries}` / `LoadErrorMsg{Dir, Err}`.
- `columns.go`: an icon column (`datatable.IconColumnWidth`, untitled,
  `fileicon.For` + `theme.IconStyle(role)` with the same directory/file roles as
  `ws`), then Name (`SizingContent`, `Search`), Size (`SizingFixed`, dim `-` for a
  directory), and Modified (`theme.TimeAgo`, `Optional`).
- Navigation: `→` enters a directory, `←`/`esc` go up (up to `/` or the volume
  root). `enter` on a file opens `uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg`, the existing path, and
  `esc` comes back. `ctrl+r` rereads. `/` opens the FilterBar.
- `N` Create (never greyed, since it acts on the browsed directory): a form in the
  viewport (Rule 112), with a **Type** field that cycles `←→` between
  `directory`/`file` (Rule 132), a **Name** field (`textinput`, validated by
  `fsbrowse.ValidName`, with the error in the footer as a Warn), and
  `[ Create ]` `[ Cancel ]` buttons. On success, reload and move the cursor to the
  new entry (`pendingSelect`).
- `D` Delete: `components.NewConfirmModal` defaulting to No. The title says "Delete
  File"/"Delete Directory", and the message gives the short path plus the number of
  entries for a non-empty directory. Execution uses
  `jobs.Start(run KindDelete owner ViewFiles, cmd)` →
  `EntryDeletedMsg` implementing `jobs.Reporter`.
- `Y` Copy the full path (existing clipboard helper in `ws`).
- `availability.go` with the `ws` pattern: `actionSet{Open, Delete, Copy, Pick}`,
  named `reason*` constants, and `guard()`. `D` is greyed on the `.` row and on a
  root. `enter` in picker mode is greyed when the row is not of the requested kind.
- Header: `GetTitle "Files"`, `GetIcon`, and `GetHeaderInfo` → `Path` =
  `theme.ShortPath(currentPath, …)` plus `Entries` = count (Rule 139). The footer
  uses FooterMessage, the FilterBar, and in picker mode the prompt as a
  `Status`. `GetHelpContent` is complete (Rule 114).
- No lowercase letter at first, so there is no `localToggles` surface. Hidden
  files follow `config.App.ShowHiddenFiles`, as in `ws`.

### Picker mode

```go
type PickKind int // PickDir, PickFile
type PickRequestMsg struct{ Kind PickKind; Start, Prompt, Tag string } // sent by the form
type PathPickedMsg  struct{ Tag, Path string }                         // received back by the form
type PickCancelledMsg struct{ Tag string }
func NewPicker(cfg *config.Config, req PickRequestMsg) Model
```

- Start: `NearestExisting(ExpandHome(req.Start))`. For a file, open its parent
  with the cursor on the file. If it is empty, start in `$HOME`.
- `PickDir`: a pseudo-row `.` (this directory) sits at the top, so the browsed
  directory can be picked even when it is empty. `enter` picks the highlighted
  directory; on a file row it is greyed.
- `PickFile`: `enter` picks the highlighted file; on a directory it is greyed and
  `→` enters it.
- `N` stays available, so a destination can be created and then picked. `esc` at
  the starting level cancels; below it, it goes up (the same logic as `ws`
  selection, `update.go:407-430`).

## 4. Router — `internal/command`, `internal/app`

- `parser.go`: `ViewFiles` plus the `viewNames` spellings `files`, `fs`.
- `command_line.go`: a `createView` case (`filebrowser.New(cfg)`), and a
  `resetSelectionModeFor` case (typing `:files` drops a lent picker).
- New `internal/app/picker.go`, **distinct from `selection.go`**, with its own
  slot `pickerReturnView`. It is separate because `:templates` can itself be lent to
  the explorer, so a picker opened from its form must not overwrite
  `selectionReturnView`.
  - `PickRequestMsg` → store `a.currentView` → install `NewPicker` into
    `a.views[ViewFiles]` (the `openBrowser` pattern without `selectionLent`).
  - `PathPickedMsg` / `PickCancelledMsg` → `currentView = pickerReturnView`, delete
    `views[ViewFiles]`, `returnToOrigin(msg)` (reused as is).
  - A single generic message pair rather than one translation per borrower: the
    borrower matches `Tag` against its own field.
- `routeWork` gets a case for `filebrowser.EntryDeletedMsg` (otherwise
  `TestEveryJobReporterIsRoutedToTheRegistry` fails).

## 5. Browse buttons in the forms

**Shared render**: `theme.RenderButton("Browse…", focused, …)` on its own line,
indented 2 cells, `●` when focused (Rule 120).

**`:cfg`** (`internal/ui/configuration`):
- A new `kindBrowse` kind in `fields.go`. A `pathField(label, ref, hint, kind)`
  constructor returns `[text field, browse field]`, where the browse field
  references the same `str` and carries `pick PickKind`. It replaces `text(...)`
  for Workspaces dir (dir), Log file (file), and the scanners' Binary (file) and
  Config (file) in `scan_fields.go:243,249`.
- `renderField`: an unfocused text field shows
  `theme.ShortPath(value, valueColumnWidth)` instead of the raw value. The focused
  one keeps the full `textinput`, which scrolls horizontally within its width.
- `update.go`: `enter` on `kindBrowse` emits `PickRequestMsg{Tag: fieldKey, Start: *str}`.
  On `PathPickedMsg` whose Tag matches, write the value (folded with `FoldHome`, so
  the YAML stays portable), validate, then `config.SaveContext` by the existing
  commit path. On a cancel, do nothing.
- The field hints and help mention `Browse`.

**`:templates`** (`internal/ui/templates/form.go`):
- A `fieldBrowse` after `fieldPath`, present in `fields()` **only for the local
  kind** (Git/OCI keep a free subdirectory or repository).
- `enter` on it emits `PickRequestMsg{Kind: PickDir, Tag: "template-path"}`, and the
  answer does `m.path.SetValue(...)`.
- `Source.Validate` / `fetch.go:106` go through `fsbrowse.ExpandHome` so that a
  typed `~/x` works.
- Unfocused rendering uses `ShortPath`.

## 6. Documentation (same commit)

- `docs/architecture/filebrowser.md` (new): the view, picker mode, the router
  contract, and `ShortPath`. Add a row to the `.claude/CLAUDE.md` Architecture table.
- `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`: the typable view list (required by
  `TestEveryTypeableViewIsDocumented`) and the view tree.
- `docs/backlog.md`: §3.95 **done**, plus an §1.1 entry for the `ws` name
  validation if it is fixed.

## Verification

Worktree: `mise run check` (fmt + vet + lint + test), then `mise run test-race`.
The existing tests that must stay green are the view contract
(`view_contract_test.go`), `keymap_test.go` / `announced_test.go`, the reporter
routing, the FooterMessage guard, and `TestEveryColumnDeclaresItsSizing`.

New tests:
- `fsbrowse`: List / Create / ValidName / Remove refusals.
- `theme/path_test.go`: ShortPath and FoldHome.
- `filebrowser`: the `ws` style (`feed` / `step` / `refused`, injected
  `EntriesLoadedMsg`). They cover →/←, the stale listing, N (valid, invalid, and
  existing name), the D confirm → `jobs.StartMsg`, and the invariant "the set of
  keys does not change between rows".
- Picker: greying of `enter` by kind, the `.` row, esc at the start level →
  `PickCancelledMsg`.
- `internal/app`: in the router harness, `PickRequestMsg` → current view = files;
  `PathPickedMsg` → return to origin, with the message received by the borrower and
  `views[ViewFiles]` deleted; and `:files` after a picker → normal view.
- `configuration` / `templates`: `enter` on Browse emits the request, and
  `PathPickedMsg` writes the value (folded) and saves.

Manually on the host (`mise run dev`):
- `:files`: navigate up to `/`, create a directory and then a file, delete them,
  and open a file in the viewer.
- `:cfg` → Workspaces dir → `↓` Browse → pick → the value appears shortened and is
  saved in `~/.devdesk/`.
- The same for a scanner's Binary, and for a local template.
- Narrow the terminal and check the fish shortening of the fields and the header.

## `internal/fsbrowse` — what a row is

It holds no git knowledge. `ws` enriches every directory with repository state
through a recursive walk, which is what a workspace listing is for and what a
listing of `/usr/lib` must not pay. What the two views share is what a row
**is**, and that is what moved here:

- **`IsHidden`** is the single rule for dot entries. `ws` calls it from its
  listing, its nested-repo walk and its fuzzy walk. One rule is the point: the
  rows `ws` shows are what `S` and `F` act on.
- **`LeadsToDir`** follows a symlink or a Windows junction (§1.3 D59). `ws`
  keeps its local `leadsToDir`/`isHidden` names as one-line delegations, so the
  walks there read unchanged.
- **`ValidName`** is one path segment: not empty, not `.`/`..`, no separator,
  no NUL. A separator is refused rather than interpreted, because `a/b` creates
  a directory the screen never showed being made, and `../x` writes outside the
  directory the screen names. `ws`'s `N` and `M` go through it too (§1.1 D79).
- **`Create`** never overwrites: `Mkdir` (not `MkdirAll`) and `O_EXCL`. A
  missing parent means the listing is stale, and that is better said than
  papered over.
- **`Remove`** refuses a filesystem root and the home directory
  (`Protected`). The view greys `D` from the same function (Rule 130), so the
  refusal can never be reached from the keyboard, only from a race.

## The view

Built like `ws`, minus the git: an icon column (Rule 125, the `directory` and
`file` roles), Name, Size (a dim `-` for a directory: its size is its inode,
not its content), and Modified. The order is `fsbrowse.List`'s — directories
first, then by name ignoring case — and there is no sort key.

**`requested` versus `currentPath`.** A navigation asks for a directory
(`requested`), and `currentPath` moves only when that listing arrives. A
listing for any other directory is dropped: two loads in flight, and this one
lost. A directory that cannot be read therefore leaves the screen on the one
that could, with the reason in the footer. The first listing is the one
exception: there is nothing to keep, so it leaves an empty table (Rule 139)
under the error.

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| `→` | enters the selected directory |
| `←` | the parent, cursor on the directory just left; nothing at a root |
| `esc` | as `←` — in a picker, cancels |
| `enter` | opens a file in the viewer — in a picker, chooses |
| `N` | a form in the viewport (Rule 112): Type (`directory`/`file`, Rule 132) and Name |
| `D` | a confirmation defaulting to No, which counts what a directory holds, then a `jobs.KindDelete` run |
| `Y` | the absolute path to the clipboard |

`D` counts entries through a Cmd (`DeletePreparedMsg`) rather than in
`Update`: it is one `ReadDir`, but on a network mount one `ReadDir` can hang,
and `Update` must not. The delete is a registry run like `ws`'s, so
`EntryDeletedMsg` is a `jobs.Reporter` with its case in `app.go`.

Hidden entries follow `app.show_hidden_files`, as in `ws`. No lowercase key
is bound, so there is no `keymap.localToggles` surface.

## The picker

```go
filebrowser.PickRequestMsg{Kind: PickDir | PickFile, Start, Prompt, Tag}  // form → router
filebrowser.PathPickedMsg{Tag, Path}                                     // router → form
filebrowser.PickCancelledMsg{Tag}                                        // router → form
```

`internal/app/picker.go` handles the request: it remembers `a.currentView` in
`pickerReturnView`, installs `filebrowser.NewPicker` as `views[ViewFiles]`, and
on either answer deletes that entry and hands the message to the borrower
through `returnToOrigin`.

**Why this is not `selection.go`.** That file translates each borrower's
request into its own vocabulary, because the explorer borrows two *different*
views to answer two *different* questions. Here the question is always "which
path", so one pair of messages serves every borrower, and `Tag` says which of
its fields the answer is for. The return slot is separate for a concrete
reason: `:templates` can itself be lent to the explorer, and a picker opened
from its form must not overwrite where that borrow returns to.

**Where it opens.** `NearestExisting(ExpandHome(Start))`. On a file, it opens
the file's directory with the cursor on the file. When nothing along the path
exists, or the field is empty, it opens `$HOME`.

**What `enter` accepts.** A row of the requested kind, and nothing else: the
other kind is greyed, and pressing it says why (Rule 130). A directory picker
puts a `.` row first — the directory being browsed — so an empty directory
can be chosen, and so can the one the picker opened on without entering
anything. `N` stays available: create the destination, then choose it.

**`esc` cancels, always.** In `:files` it goes up. In a picker, whose scope is
the whole filesystem, there is no "starting level" whose meaning survives `←`,
so `esc` cancels from anywhere, and `←` is the only way up.

`InEditMode` is true for a picker: its `esc` answers the borrower, and a bare
`q` or `:` must not leave the view with the borrower still waiting. `ctrl+p`
still works. A command typed there abandons the picker, and
`resetSelectionModeFor(ViewFiles)` drops it, so the next `:files` is the
browser and not the orphaned picker.

### The borrowers

| Form | Field | Kind | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:cfg` app | Workspaces dir | dir | `/Workspaces dir` |
| `:cfg` app | Log file | file | `/Log file` |
| `:cfg` tools | each scanner's Binary | file | `<tool>/Binary` |
| `:cfg` tools | Config (rules file), when the tool has one | file | `<tool>/Config` |
| `:templates` form | Directory, local source only | dir | `template-path` |

**`:cfg`.** `pathField(label, ref, hint, kind)` returns two rows: the text
field (`path: true`) and a `kindBrowse` row sharing its accessor and label.
The label is what the answer is matched by (`pickTag` = tool + label, since
every scanner has a "Binary"), and it cannot widen the chevron column, which
the text field already sets. `enter` means nothing anywhere else in this view,
and it is greyed off a Browse row. The answer goes through the field's `Apply`
then `persist`, the path a typed value takes.

It is written **absolute, not folded to `~`**. `config.ExpandPaths` runs once,
at load, and the session reads what is in memory. A `~/bin/trivy` written
here would reach the scanner unexpanded until the next start. The form
shortens it on screen anyway.

**`:templates`.** `fieldBrowse` is in `fields()` for the local kind only: a git
subdirectory or an OCI repository is not a path on this machine. `fetch.go`
expands `~` before handing the directory to `git archive`, so a typed
`~/templates/x` works too.

A Browse row has no key of its own for a reason: every key a text field could
claim is also a character a path can contain.

## Short paths — `theme.ShortPath(path, maxWidth)`

What gives way, in order of what matters least:

1. `$HOME` → `~`, always (`FoldHome`, which used to be `security`'s private
   `shortenHome`);
2. intermediate segments reduced to their first rune, left to right, **stopping
   as soon as the path fits**. A dot segment keeps its dot: `.config` becomes
   `.c`, because a lone `c` names a different directory;
3. only then `TruncateTailWidth` — the `...` prefix — when even the fully
   reduced form is too wide.

The last segment is never reduced: it is the name the field is about. Widths
are measured with `runewidth`, not `len`.

```
~/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk   fits
~/p/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk          one reduced
~/p/w/a/devdesk                               all reduced
...a/devdesk                                  head cut
```

Where it is used: a `:cfg` path field at rest (the value column's width), the
templates form's local directory at rest (60 cells), the `:files` header's
Path (48), and the `N` form's title. A field being edited always shows the
whole path. The dashboard's `truncatePath` predates this and still keeps only
the tail; converging it is left for later.

**Vérifications.** Le lint ne relève aucun problème. Tous les tests des paquets modifiés passent, y compris avec le détecteur de concurrence, ainsi que les tests de contrat qui contraignent les vues et le clavier. Je n'ai pas lancé l'application dans un vrai terminal : j'ai seulement regardé le rendu de la table et du formulaire `N` depuis un test.

**Ce qui a été fait :**
- **La vue `:files`** parcourt tout le système de fichiers. Elle s'ouvre dans `$HOME`, `→` entre dans un répertoire et `←` remonte jusqu'à `/`, curseur sur le répertoire qu'on vient de quitter.
  - `N` ouvre un formulaire : type `directory`/`file` à choisir avec ←→, puis le nom.
  - `D` demande confirmation, avec Non par défaut, et indique combien d'entrées contient le répertoire. Il est grisé sur `/` et sur `$HOME`.
  - `Y` copie le chemin, `enter` ouvre un fichier dans le visualiseur.
- **Le sélecteur** : `↓` jusqu'au bouton Browse, puis `enter`, ouvre la même vue là où pointe le champ (ou dans le dossier existant le plus proche).
  - `enter` choisit une entrée du bon type, l'autre type est grisé.
  - Quand on demande un répertoire, une première ligne `.` désigne le répertoire courant, même vide.
  - `esc` revient au formulaire sans rien changer.
  - Il est branché sur les champs Workspaces dir, Log file, et Binary et Config de chaque scanner dans `:cfg`, ainsi que sur le répertoire d'un template local dans `:templates`.
- **Chemins abrégés** : `$HOME` devient `~`, puis les dossiers intermédiaires sont réduits à leur première lettre, de gauche à droite, jusqu'à ce que le chemin tienne. Le nom final reste entier. Pendant l'édition, le champ montre le chemin complet.

**Écarts par rapport au plan :**
- **Chemin enregistré en absolu, pas en `~/…`.** La config ne remplace `~` qu'au démarrage : un `~/bin/trivy` enregistré aurait été transmis tel quel au scanner jusqu'au redémarrage suivant. L'écran l'affiche quand même abrégé.
- **`esc` annule toujours dans le sélecteur**, même après être remonté, puisqu'il n'y a pas de racine fixe. Dans `:files`, `esc` remonte d'un niveau.

**Défaut corrigé au passage (D79).** Dans `ws`, `N` et `M` acceptaient `a/b` ou `../x` comme nom : on pouvait créer des dossiers imbriqués ou écrire hors du répertoire affiché. Les deux vérifient maintenant que le nom est un seul élément de chemin, et j'ai ajouté des tests.

# Files — the browser, the picker, and short paths

> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
> read this file when working on the code it describes.

`:files` (alias `:fs`) browses the whole filesystem, and a form's **Browse**
button borrows the same view as a path picker (§3.95). Three packages:

| Package | Holds |
|---|---|
`resetSelectionModeFor(ViewFiles)` drops it, so the next `:files` is the
browser and not the orphaned picker.

### The borrowers

| Form | Field | Kind | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:cfg` app | Workspaces dir | dir | `/Workspaces dir` |
| `:cfg` app | Log file | file | `/Log file` |
| `:cfg` tools | each scanner's Binary | file | `<tool>/Binary` |
| `:cfg` tools | Config (rules file), when the tool has one | file | `<tool>/Config` |
| `:templates` form | Directory, local source only | dir | `template-path` |

**`:cfg`.** `pathField(label, ref, hint, kind)` returns two rows: the text
field (`path: true`) and a `kindBrowse` row sharing its accessor and label.
The label is what the answer is matched by (`pickTag` = tool + label, since
every scanner has a "Binary"), and it cannot widen the chevron column, which
the text field already sets. `enter` means nothing anywhere else in this view,
and it is greyed off a Browse row. The answer goes through the field's `Apply`
then `persist`, the path a typed value takes.

It is written **absolute, not folded to `~`**. `config.ExpandPaths` runs once,
at load, and the session reads what is in memory. A `~/bin/trivy` written
here would reach the scanner unexpanded until the next start. The form
shortens it on screen anyway.

**`:templates`.** `fieldBrowse` is in `fields()` for the local kind only: a git
subdirectory or an OCI repository is not a path on this machine. `fetch.go`
expands `~` before handing the directory to `git archive`, so a typed
`~/templates/x` works too.

A Browse row has no key of its own for a reason: every key a text field could
claim is also a character a path can contain.

content.text:
Je te le déconseille : ça coûte cher pour un gain partiel. Mes arguments viennent du code et de la doc des plateformes ; je n'ai rien prototypé.

**Ce que ça couvrirait, et ce que ça ne couvrirait pas**

On ne surveillerait que `.git/` de chaque dépôt affiché, pas son arbre de travail :

| Changement fait ailleurs | Détecté ? |
|---|---|
| `pull`, `fetch`, `commit`, `checkout`, nouveau tag | oui : Last Tag, branche, ⇡⇣ |
| `git add` | oui, via `.git/index` (piégé, voir plus bas) |
| Un fichier modifié ou créé dans l'éditeur (`!N`, `?N`) | **non** : l'éditeur ne touche pas `.git/` |

Suivre aussi l'arbre de travail demanderait une surveillance récursive de tout le dépôt, `node_modules` et `.venv` compris : des milliers de surveillances sous Linux. Hors de question. La colonne Git Status resterait donc à moitié périmée, et `ctrl+r` resterait nécessaire pour elle.

**Le piège : DevDesk se déclencherait lui-même**

`git status --porcelain`, que `ws` lance pour chaque dépôt, réécrit souvent `.git/index` en rafraîchissant les infos de fichiers. Si on surveille `index`, chaque relecture déclenche un événement, qui déclenche une relecture, et ainsi de suite. Il faudrait ignorer `index`, et donc perdre `git add`, ou ignorer les événements causés par nos propres relectures. En plus, un seul `pull` produit une rafale d'événements (verrous, `FETCH_HEAD`, `ORIG_HEAD`, refs) : il faudrait les regrouper par dépôt sur environ 300 ms. Chaque relecture relance 7 processus git : sous Windows, cela fait environ 0,2 à 0,4 s par dépôt.

**Plateformes (goreleaser publie pour Linux, macOS et Windows)**

| | Mécanisme | Risque |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | inotify | faible : ta limite est de 65 536 surveillances |
| **macOS** | kqueue : **un descripteur de fichier ouvert par élément surveillé** | réel : la limite par défaut d'un terminal est 256 descripteurs. Un niveau de 60 dépôts × 3 dossiers, plus ce que DevDesk ouvre déjà, s'en approche |
| Windows natif (ton cas pour `sentinel`) | ReadDirectoryChangesW | bon en local, peu fiable sur un partage réseau |
| **WSL sur `/mnt/c`** | inotify sur drvfs | **aucun événement** pour un changement fait côté Windows : la fonctionnalité serait muette, sans rien dire |

Il faudrait aussi gérer les dépôts « worktree », où `.git` est un fichier qui pointe ailleurs : les refs vivent alors dans le répertoire git commun, à résoudre par dépôt.

**Architecture : c'est ce qui pèse le plus**

- Le modèle de `ws` est copié à chaque `Update` ; il ne peut pas posséder de surveillance vivante sans casser la règle 110.
- Le routeur **supprime** des vues sans prévenir : `delete(a.views, …)` sur `:workspaces`, au retour d'une sélection, et quand on change de contexte, où toutes les vues sont reconstruites. Il n'existe aucun point où une vue peut se nettoyer. Une surveillance tenue par la vue fuirait donc des goroutines et des descripteurs.
- La forme propre serait un **service tenu par le routeur**, sur le modèle du registre `internal/jobs` : un seul watcher pour toute l'application. `ws` déclarerait l'ensemble des dépôts affichés à chaque listing, et le routeur transmettrait des messages `RepoChangedMsg{Path}` à la vue. C'est un nouveau composant transverse, avec son cycle de vie lié aux changements de contexte.
- Les tests aussi : des événements réels du système de fichiers sont lents et instables, il faudrait une interface injectable et un faux watcher.

**Dépendance**

`github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify` n'est pas dans `go.mod` aujourd'hui, même en indirect. C'est une bibliothèque petite et maintenue, et sa seule dépendance, `golang.org/x/sys`, y est déjà. Là-dessus, rien de bloquant.

**En résumé**

| | |
|---|---|
| Gain | Last Tag, branche et ⇡⇣ à jour sans `ctrl+r`, mais seulement pour les changements faits *pendant* que la vue affiche ce niveau |
| Ce qui reste périmé | `!N` / `?N` |

Le rapport coût/gain est mauvais, puisque l'entrée dans la vue et les changements de niveau relisent déjà tout. Si le besoin revient, l'alternative la moins chère est une relecture limitée aux dépôts **visibles**, déclenchée quand le terminal reprend le focus. Bubble Tea sait envoyer un message à ce moment-là, sans aucune surveillance à entretenir, et ça couvre le scénario « j'ai fait un `pull` dans l'autre fenêtre, je reviens ».
